answer: Price the cohort, not the account. Wallets registered from one subnet within 12 epochs form a cohort of size c; each member locks a inlet fee of 3*c POA for 30 epochs. N=1 costs 3; N=40 costs 40*(3*40)=4,800 POA, and fees cannot be pooled. A gale panel of 4 reviewers samples 1 in 8 cohorts per epoch and posts results in the quill log; a fake loses its fee. An honest user alone locks 3 POA and gets it back. A wrongly grouped user appeals within 5 epochs for a refund. It fails if attackers use thousands of subnets.
